newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLO/Bund spread expected to widen again.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLO/Bund spread expected to widen again.

text.p: The yield spread between 10-year Belgian linear bonds and Bunds, which narrowed on Tuesday due to a stronger Belgian franc and dollar on the mark, is bound to widen again the next few days, dealers said.
The spread was down at seven basis points against 11 on Monday.
"It will be hard to keep the spread at these levels, it will go out to 10 or higher again because in fact nothing has been solved on the (Belgian) political front," a trader said.
"People are buying Belgium a little again now that the franc has recovered," he said.
The franc had been under pressure last month due to a string of scandals involving prominent members of the francophone socialist party PS, one of four government coalition parties.
But the pressure started waning last week, lifting the franc back to near the midpoint of 20.6255 to the mark. It was at 20.6275/90 against 20.6320/35 on Monday.
Traders noted the market remained very illiquid, which exacerbated the impact of major purchases. "A few big buys and the spread immediately goes down," one said.
Business was mainly focusing on the benchmark OLO but he also noted large blocks "of a couple of billions" at the short end in OLO 13.
But end-investors continued to shun the market, he added.
Traders noted that the franc's recovery was also fuelled by the dollar's strength on the mark.
"Everybody's selling marks now, which is always good for the franc, and the French franc, even the lira," one said. "But that is purely technical, not the result of political considerations."
Traders were now awaiting the release of German and U.S. employment data. U.S. data are due out on Friday. "But the German ones are at least as important," one trader said.
German Bild am Sonntag newspaper said on Sunday that German unemployment rose by 120,000 to a postwar record of 4.8 million in February, lifting the rate to 12.5 percent from January's 12.2 percent.
It did not give a source for the February figures which will be officially released by the Federal Labour Office on Thursday.
